correct_feedback: Yes! In stanza two the spring rain comes and the seed wakes up. That's the moment the story starts to change and grow.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, look at stanza two again. What new thing happens after the rain arrives? Think about how the seed is different now.
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it shows the seed starting to wake up and change. The spring rain comes and the little seed wakes up one day.

correct_feedback: Great thinking! Scene two is at the park and scene three is at the shelter, so in between Ana had to travel there to get the puppy.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Notice where scene two happens and where scene three happens. How did Ana get from one place to the other?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that Ana traveled from the park to the animal shelter. Scene two is at the park and scene three is at the shelter, so she had to go there.

correct_feedback: Exactly! The weather keeps changing, but that last line stays the same to show the speaker keeps on waiting no matter what.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. The weather changes in each stanza, but one line stays exactly the same. What might the poet want that repeated line to show?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that the speaker keeps waiting no matter what changes. The repeated line stays the same even while rain, snow, and sun come and go.

correct_feedback: Nice work! A storm, then alone on an island, then a sail coming closer tells a story of a boy stranded who might get rescued.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Read the three titles in order. What does each one hint about, and how might the whole adventure unfold?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that a boy is caught in a storm, ends up stranded, and may finally be rescued. The three titles tell that story in order.

correct_feedback: Yes! In the fourth stanza the bright light turns and guides the lost ship to safe harbor. That's the lighthouse's most important job.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. A lighthouse is built to help ships. In which stanza does the light actually guide a ship to safety?
reveal_feedback: The answer is the fourth stanza. That's where the bright light turns and guides the lost ship to safe harbor, its most important job.

correct_feedback: Great! The narrator thinks vegetables are boring, but you enjoy some, so your point of view is different from the narrator's.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, think about what the narrator believes and how you really feel. Which choice shows a view that is truly different from theirs?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that your point of view is different, because you enjoy eating some vegetables. That's the opposite of the narrator finding them boring.

correct_feedback: Exactly right! You think cheating is wrong and the character thinks it's okay, so the two of you have different points of view.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. You believe one thing and the character believes something else. What do we call it when two people think differently?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that you and the character have different points of view. You think cheating is wrong, but the character thinks it's okay.

correct_feedback: Yes! The narrator tells us a puddle is hiding ahead, but Mia doesn't know it's there. That's the secret only the reader gets.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. The narrator shares one thing that Mia herself cannot see. Reread the sentence and find what's hiding from her.
reveal_feedback: The answer is that a small puddle is hiding just ahead. The narrator tells the reader this, but Mia does not know it's there.

correct_feedback: Well done! The wolf and the pigs each tell the story their own way, so the reader gets to decide what really happened.
incorrect_feedback: Not yet. Each side tells a different story. Instead of picking who's for sure right, think about what a smart reader gets to do.
reveal_feedback: The answer is that both characters have their own version of events, and the reader can decide. Each side tells it differently.

correct_feedback: Yes! The words don't mention a party, but the balloons, streamers, and cake in the picture show a celebration is happening.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, look at what's in the picture. Balloons, streamers, and a big cake are clues. What kind of event has all those things?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that there's a party or celebration happening. The balloons, streamers, and cake in the picture show it, even though the words don't.

correct_feedback: Great! The tiny flashlight, worried eyes, and long dark shadows make the hallway feel even more mysterious and a little scary.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Picture the dark shadows and Leo's worried, wide eyes. What kind of feeling does that add to the spooky hallway?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it makes the hallway seem even more mysterious and a little scary. The shadows and Leo's worried face add to that feeling.

correct_feedback: Exactly! The words say fine, but the tears in the picture show the character really isn't. So they're hiding their true feelings.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. The words and the picture don't match. If someone says fine but has tears, what might that tell us?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that the character is lying about their feelings. They say they're fine, but the tears in the picture show they really aren't.

correct_feedback: Yes! Her big joyful smile, sparkling eyes, and shared drawing show that Lily is a cheerful, outgoing friend.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Think about what kind of PERSON Lily is, not just small details. What do her smile and sparkling eyes tell you?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it makes it clear Lily is a cheerful and outgoing friend. Her joyful smile and sparkling eyes show her personality.

correct_feedback: Nice! The huge trees and tall mountains next to the little cottage make it look even smaller. The picture adds that big feeling.
incorrect_feedback: Not yet. The cottage is small, and the picture puts it beside giant trees and mountains. What does that make you notice about its size?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it emphasizes how small the cottage is compared to nature. The huge trees and mountains make it look even tinier.

correct_feedback: Yes! The words only say Maya put on her coat, but the snow and snowman in the picture show it's cold and snowy outside.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, look at the picture. Snow is falling and there's a big snowman. What does that tell you about the weather?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it is cold and snowy outside. The falling snow and the snowman in the picture show us that.

correct_feedback: Great! The words just say Ben looked in the box, but the picture shows a fluffy puppy sitting inside it.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Look closely at what's shown inside the box in the picture. What is sitting in there?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that there is a puppy in the box. The picture shows a fluffy puppy sitting right inside it.

correct_feedback: Yes! The picture shows sand, water, and a sandcastle, so we know the kids are playing at the beach.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Look at where the kids are in the picture. They're building a sandcastle by the water. What place has sand and water?
reveal_feedback: The answer is at the beach. The picture shows the kids building a sandcastle by the water, which tells us where they are.

correct_feedback: Nice! The words just say Grandpa smiled, but the cake with candles and the party hat show it's his birthday.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. Grandpa is holding a cake with candles and wearing a party hat. What special day has those things?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it is Grandpa's birthday. The cake with candles and the party hat in the picture show us that.

correct_feedback: Yes! The lamp, the dark window, and the moon in the picture tell us Lily is reading at night.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, look at the picture. There's a lamp on and the moon is out the window. What time of day shows a moon and darkness?
reveal_feedback: The answer is at night. The lamp, the dark window, and the moon in the picture show that it's nighttime.

correct_feedback: Great! Both stories share the same friendship lesson, but one is near big buildings and one is on a farm. The places are different.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Both stories teach about friendship and have two friends. Look for the part that really changes between them.
reveal_feedback: The answer is the places they happen. One story is near big buildings and a busy park, the other is on a farm, but both teach friendship.

correct_feedback: Yes! It's the same girl and same author, but now she solves a mystery at a museum instead of school. The setting and plot changed.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. The same girl and same author are in both. What is new in the second story, the place and what happens?
reveal_feedback: The answer is the setting and specific plot. The girl and author stay the same, but the mystery moves from her school to a museum.

correct_feedback: Exactly! Rosie learns about kindness in one story and asking for help in the other. The lesson is what's different.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Rosie is in both stories, but she learns something different in each. What part of a story is the lesson it teaches?
reveal_feedback: The answer is the lesson or message. In one story Rosie learns to be kind, and in the other she learns it's okay to ask for help.

correct_feedback: Well done! Mira refused help in both stories and things went wrong both times. The shared lesson is that going it alone can bring trouble.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, think about what Mira did in BOTH stories and how each ended badly. What did refusing everyone's help lead to?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that trying to do everything alone can lead to trouble. Mira refused help in both stories, and both times things went wrong.

correct_feedback: Yes! Scout is calm on the farm but busy and barky in the city. The author shows how a new setting can change how a character acts.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Notice how Scout acts differently after he moves. Why might the author change where Scout lives?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that a new setting can change how a character acts. Scout is calm on the farm but busy and barky in the city.

correct_feedback: Great thinking! In both tales the fox tricks another animal, then gets tricked right back. That's the pattern the plots share.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Follow what the fox does in each story, then what happens to the fox after. What pattern repeats in both?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that the fox tricks someone, and then gets tricked back. That same pattern happens in both tales.

correct_feedback: Yes! Kai's machines fail again and again but finally work. Both stories share the big idea that if you keep trying, you can succeed.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. In both stories Kai fails many times before it works. What big idea does that teach the reader?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that if you keep trying, you can succeed. Both of Kai's machines fail many times before they finally work.

correct_feedback: Nice! Rosa returns a lost pet in both stories, but one is in a snowy town and one in a desert. Same kind deed, different place.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Rosa does the same helpful thing in both, but the settings change. Which sentence captures both the same AND the different part?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that Rosa does the same kind deed, but in a different place. She returns a lost pet in both, one snowy, one a desert.

correct_feedback: Yes! The place changes from park to beach, but Max is the main character in both stories. He stays the same.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, one thing stays exactly the same in both stories while the place changes. Who is in both stories?
reveal_feedback: The answer is the main character, Max. He's in both stories, even though the place changes from park to beach.

correct_feedback: Great! Pip is the same dog with the same author, but he lives on a farm in one story and a city in the other. The place is different.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Pip the dog and the author stay the same. Look for the one thing that changes between the two stories.
reveal_feedback: The answer is the place where Pip lives. He lives on a farm in one story and in a city in the other.

correct_feedback: Yes! Both stories about Lily teach the same lesson, be kind to others. That's what the two stories share.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Both stories teach the very same thing about being kind. What do the two stories have in common?
reveal_feedback: The answer is the same lesson. Both stories about Lily teach be kind to others.

correct_feedback: Nice! In both stories Sam is looking for something lost, a toy in one and a hat in the other. That's what's alike.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. In both stories Sam is doing the same thing. What is Sam trying to do in each one?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that Sam is looking for something lost. In one story it's a toy and in the other a hat, but both are about searching.

correct_feedback: Yes! One story is in winter with snow and the other in summer at the pool. The setting, when and where, is different.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, one story is winter and one is summer, in different places. What do we call the when and where of a story?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that the setting is different. One story happens in winter with snow and the other in summer at the pool.

correct_feedback: Great! Putting out a lantern every night to guide others shows the old woman is thoughtful and wants to help people.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Think about WHY someone would put a light in the window every single night. What kind of person does that show she is?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that she is a thoughtful person who wants to help others. Lighting a lantern every night helps guide people.

correct_feedback: Yes! Diego started over when his supplies ran out and kept going all week. That shows he's persistent and creative despite setbacks.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Diego ran out of supplies and had to start over, but he kept working all week. What does that tell you about him?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that he was persistent and creative despite setbacks. He started over when supplies ran out and never gave up.

correct_feedback: Yes! Even after the kids said she couldn't, Sana grabbed a branch and started to climb. She didn't let them stop her.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. Right after the kids doubted her, what did Sana do? Reread that part to find her next action.
reveal_feedback: The answer is that she grabbed a branch and started to climb. Even after the kids said she couldn't, she went for it.

correct_feedback: Great! A mysterious package from your future self makes readers wonder what's inside. The author wants us curious and intrigued.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. A strange package sits for days and says it's from your future self. What feeling does that mystery give the reader?
reveal_feedback: The answer is curious and intrigued. The mysterious package from Eliot's future self makes the reader wonder what's inside.

correct_feedback: Yes! Everyone expected ghosts, but Lina found raccoons instead. That surprising, funny twist is what makes the ending work.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Everyone thought ghosts, but Lina found something silly instead. What kind of ending catches the reader off guard?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it surprises the reader with a funny, unexpected twist. Everyone expected ghosts, but it was raccoons.

correct_feedback: Well done! Maya was about to speak but chose kindness instead, deciding not to make Sam feel bad about the accident.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, Maya opens her mouth, then closes it and says something nice about Sam's drawing. Why might she hold back her first words?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that she decides not to make Sam feel bad about the accident. She holds back and chooses kind words instead.

correct_feedback: Yes! Priya wanted a different name but clapped and helped anyway. That shows she can accept a group decision even when she loses.
incorrect_feedback: Almost. Priya wanted Shelly but still helped and said everyone gets a say. What does that show about how she handles losing a vote?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that she can accept a group decision even when it isn't what she wanted. She wanted Shelly but supported the class.

correct_feedback: Great! The old dog naps in the shade while the pup runs quick and new. The poem shows the pup is lively and the dog is now slow with age.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look. The old dog rests while the pup runs and plays. What is the poem mainly showing about these two dogs?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that the pup is young and lively while the old dog is now slow with age. The dog rests while the pup runs about.

correct_feedback: Yes! Grandpa smiles at Grandma's garden and pours her cup each day. He's remembering her and keeping her close in his routine.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Grandma passed away, yet Grandpa still sets out her cup and smiles at her garden. Why might he keep doing this each morning?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that he is remembering Grandma and keeping her close in his routine. The second cup is a way to honor her each day.

correct_feedback: Nice! Omar bragged and blamed the word at first, but that night he quietly practiced. He stops bragging and starts working to get better.
incorrect_feedback: Close one. Compare how Omar acts at the start with what he does that night. How is he different by the end?
reveal_feedback: The answer is that he stops bragging and quietly starts working to get better. At first he boasted, but that night he practiced alone.

correct_feedback: Great listening! The text says the Amazon makes about 20 percent of the world's oxygen and is home to more than 10 million kinds of plants and animals.
incorrect_feedback: Hmm, listen again for the two numbers in the text, the percent of oxygen and how many kinds of plants and animals. Match them both carefully.
reveal_feedback: The answer is that it makes about 20 percent of the world's oxygen and has more than 10 million types of plants and animals, just as the text said.

correct_feedback: Yes! The text says Harriet Tubman led about 70 people to freedom through the Underground Railroad.
incorrect_feedback: Good try. Go back to the text and find the exact number of people Harriet Tubman led to freedom. Read that part slowly.
reveal_feedback: The answer is about 70. The text says Harriet Tubman led about 70 people to freedom through the Underground Railroad.

correct_feedback: Yes! The text explains that earthquakes happen when tectonic plates, big pieces of Earth's crust, suddenly move.
incorrect_feedback: Take another look at the text. It names one thing that suddenly moves and causes earthquakes. Find that cause in the words.
reveal_feedback: The answer is tectonic plates suddenly moving. The text says earthquakes happen when these large pieces of Earth's crust suddenly move.
